paper.title: Concentration & asymptotics of the sample mean
paper.description: A synthetic theoretical statistics example created for Proof Map. It does not reproduce a published paper. All numbering, page locations, and evidence excerpts belong to this illustrative document; relationship verification has not been performed.

nodes.label: Assumption 1.1
nodes.title: Independent observations
nodes.statement: Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent and identically distributed real-valued random variables with $\mathbb{E}X_i=\mu$ and $0<v=\operatorname{Var}(X_i)<\infty$.

nodes.label: Definition 1.2
nodes.title: Sample mean
nodes.statement:
The sample mean is the estimator
$$\bar X_n=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i.$$

nodes.label: Definition 1.3
nodes.title: Sub-Gaussian variable
nodes.statement:
A centered random variable $Z$ is $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian if, for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$,
$$\mathbb{E}e^{\lambda Z}\leq e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.$$ Here $\sigma>0$ is a variance-proxy parameter.

nodes.label: Assumption 1.4
nodes.title: Sub-Gaussian noise
nodes.statement: In addition to Assumption 1.1, each centered observation $X_i-\mu$ is $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian in the sense of Definition 1.3, with the same known parameter $\sigma>0$.

nodes.label: Lemma 2.2
nodes.title: Chernoff bound
nodes.statement:
For any real random variable $Z$, any $t>0$, and any $\lambda>0$ for which the expectation is finite,
$$\mathbb{P}(Z\geq t)\leq e^{-\lambda t}\mathbb{E}e^{\lambda Z}.$$ Apply the same inequality to $-Z$ for the lower tail.

nodes.label: Theorem 2.3
nodes.title: Finite-sample concentration
nodes.statement:
Under Assumptions 1.1 and 1.4, the sample mean satisfies, for every $t>0$,
$$\mathbb{P}\!\left(|\bar X_n-\mu|\geq t\right)\leq 2\exp\!\left(-\frac{nt^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).$$
The conclusion is nonasymptotic and holds for every integer $n\geq1$.

evidence.excerpt: Combine Lemma 2.1 with Lemma 2.2, optimize over the positive parameter, and apply a union bound to the two tails.

nodes.label: Corollary 2.4
nodes.title: A confidence interval
nodes.statement:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem 2.3, for $0<\alpha<1$, the interval
$$I_n=\left[\bar X_n-\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2/\alpha)}{n}},\;\bar X_n+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2/\alpha)}{n}}\right]$$
satisfies $\mathbb{P}(\mu\in I_n)\geq1-\alpha$.

nodes.label: Lemma 3.1
nodes.title: Variance of the average
nodes.statement:
Under Assumption 1.1,
$$\mathbb{E}\bar X_n=\mu,\qquad\operatorname{Var}(\bar X_n)=\frac{v}{n}.$$
The variance identity follows because the centered cross terms have zero expectation.

nodes.label: Proposition 3.2
nodes.title: Mean-square consistency
nodes.statement:
Under Assumption 1.1,
$$\mathbb{E}(\bar X_n-\mu)^2=\frac{v}{n}\longrightarrow0.$$
In particular, $\bar X_n\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}\mu$ by Chebyshev's inequality.

nodes.label: Theorem 3.3
nodes.title: Asymptotic normality
nodes.statement:
Under Assumption 1.1 alone, the classical i.i.d. central limit theorem yields
$$\frac{\sqrt{n}(\bar X_n-\mu)}{\sqrt{v}}\xrightarrow{d}\mathcal{N}(0,1).$$
No sub-Gaussian assumption is required. This is a limiting distribution statement, not a finite-sample tail bound.

nodes.label: Example 4.1
nodes.title: Gaussian observations
nodes.statement: If $X_i\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)$ independently, then $X_i-\mu$ is $\sigma^2$-sub-Gaussian with equality in the MGF inequality. Moreover, $\bar X_n\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2/n)$ exactly.

nodes.label: Claim 4.2
nodes.title: Finite variance is enough?
nodes.statement: Candidate claim (false): every centered finite-variance random variable is sub-Gaussian for some finite variance proxy. Counterexample 4.3 refutes this assertion.

nodes.label: Counterexample 4.3
nodes.title: Heavy-tailed observations
nodes.statement: A Student $t$ random variable with three degrees of freedom has mean zero and variance $3$, but its MGF is infinite for every nonzero real parameter. It is therefore not sub-Gaussian. Independent copies satisfy Assumption 1.1 but not Assumption 1.4.

source.location: Section 4, finite variance without exponential tails

nodes.label: Proposition 3.4
nodes.title: Normalized mean-square error
nodes.statement:
Under Assumption 1.1, the unbiasedness of $\bar X_n$ makes the variance formula of Lemma 3.1 equivalent to
$$\mathbb{E}\left[\bigl(\sqrt{n}(\bar X_n-\mu)\bigr)^2\right]=v.$$

nodes.label: Remark A.1
nodes.title: Beyond the sample mean
nodes.statement: Robust mean estimators can be studied under weaker tail assumptions. This observation is not used by any result in this illustrative document and has no recorded relationships.
